summary: Revision 1 of 3: add one additive option to the existing per-button configuration. `focusSheen?: boolean` (default false) goes on the already-exported `ZestCustomProps` that is passed as the `zest` prop; because `useZestConfig` merges provider defaultProps, semantic defaults and local zest, the field flows through with no new plumbing and no change to `UI/index.ts`. The streak is pure CSS, no React state, listeners or timers: a regular button gets `.sheenFocus` and a `::after` layer clipped by the button's existing position:relative/overflow:hidden/border-radius; a split button gets `.sheenFocus` on `.splitButtonContainer`, which gains position:relative, and a matching `::after` layer over the whole control. Keyboard-only is done with `.button.sheenFocus:focus-visible::after` for regular and `.splitButtonContainer.sheenFocus:has(:focus-visible)::after` for split, so a mouse click (plain :focus) does not fire and moving between the two segments of one split control does not restart the sweep. The band is a 45-degree background gradient that travels top-right to bottom-left in about 0.6s, one sweep, ending transparent. Deliberate deviation from the request's wording: the split wrapper is NOT given overflow:hidden, because the focus ring is an outer box-shadow on each segment and a clipping wrapper would cut it (R5 requires both rings fully visible); instead the overlay's own border-radius (var(--zest-radius-md)) clips the band, which also stays inside the wrapper so it can never cover the outward ring. Colour follows R4: solid keeps white at about 65% (matching the chevron streak); outline/text/dashed set `--zest-sheen-color` from color-mix(currentColor, ~70%) so the band follows each style, variant and the forced light/dark classes instead of being white-on-white; for the split overlay, which cannot inherit currentColor from a sibling segment, the wrapper gets the flat/success/danger marker classes and the existing force-light/force-dark classes so the same `--zest-color-*-bg` tokens pick the right accent. When `.sheenFocus` is on a split wrapper, `.sheenFocus .dropdownTrigger::before` is disabled so the chevron mount streak and the whole-control streak never play together (A2). Everything is removed under prefers-reduced-motion (A1). Scale/resource: O(1) work per focus arrival, one pseudo-element, no render-path work that grows with data, no state/listeners/timers/network/storage, no layout or size change (the layer is absolutely positioned), no new dependency; only a small CSS addition to the already-injected module, so startup and memory are unchanged. `.size-limit.json` does not exist, so no budget is changed. Public surface: one optional field is added to an existing exported type; no export is added, removed or changed, so this is non-breaking and needs no breaking-changes entry or version bump.

touches: UI/ZestButton.tsx (new optional focusSheen field, class wiring for regular and split)
Styles/ZestButton.module.css (sheen layer, keyframes, colour rules, split wrapper position, mount-streak suppression, reduced motion)
README.md and documentation/* (prop and feature documentation)
reuses: existing `.button` position:relative, overflow:hidden and border-radius:var(--zest-radius-md) for the regular-button clip
existing `.splitButtonContainer` wrapper and its ZestDropdownMenu chevron trigger
existing `force-light`/`force-dark` theme classes and `--zest-color-*-bg` variables for theme-aware band colour
existing chevron mount-streak sweep technique (background gradient + background-position keyframes) and the existing `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block
existing `useZestConfig` provider/semantic/local merge so focusSheen needs no new context or hook
existing CSS Modules injection and the Jest pattern of parsing the CSS module source for selector assertions
adds: `focusSheen?: boolean` field on the exported `ZestCustomProps` (no new export)
`.sheenFocus`, `.sheenFlat`, `.sheenSuccess`, `.sheenDanger` CSS classes and `zestFocusSheen` keyframes in the existing stylesheet
new `docs/features/zest-button-focus-sheen/guide.md` plus edits to the existing documentation pages and README

additions.title: Turn the focus streak off for reduced motion
additions.why: People who ask their device to reduce motion should not get a sweeping band.
acceptance: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, keyboard-focusing an opted-in regular or split button plays no streak and leaves no visible band.
Without that preference the streak still plays, for both regular and split buttons.

additions.title: Suppress the chevron mount streak when the focus streak is enabled
additions.why: Two streaks on one split control would collide and look like a glitch.
acceptance: An opted-in split button shows no chevron mount streak on first paint, on any button style, variant or theme.
A split button that is not opted in keeps its chevron mount streak exactly as today.

additions.title: Characterisation tests for the existing button appearance and chevron streak
additions.why: The shared stylesheet is being edited, so the behaviour already shipped is pinned before the change.
acceptance: Tests record the current class list of a plain regular button and of a split wrapper/button and pass before the change.
Tests record the existing chevron mount-streak rule and focus-ring rule and still pass after the change.
A button that does not pass focusSheen renders no sheen class and keeps the same DOM and behaviour.

additions.title: Document the focus streak on every page readers use
additions.why: A new prop that cannot be found is a feature nobody can use.
acceptance: documentation/api.md lists focusSheen on ZestCustomProps with its default and both regular and split usage.
documentation/features.md and documentation/examples.md show the option on a regular button and a split button.
documentation/configuration.md notes that the provider's defaultProps can set it app-wide, and README links to the new guide.
The new docs/features/zest-button-focus-sheen/guide.md explains keyboard-only focus, clipping, colours per style/theme and reduced motion.
